citations.A1: the cache is written once and has no invalidation condition — `_cache is None` is only ever true once per process, so nothing can ever re-read the file; fix by storing a version stamp alongside the value and re-reading when it changes
citations.A2: NOT a fix — a TTL/time-based expiry: it shortens the stale window but still serves known-wrong values for up to the TTL
citations.A3: NOT a fix — exposing a `reload_config()` for callers to call: it makes correctness depend on every call site knowing when an external process wrote the file
citations.A4: The cache is not keyed by `path`, so `get_config('a.json')` then `get_config('b.json')` returns a's contents; key the cache dict by the resolved absolute path.
citations.A5: adding a lock: it makes concurrent first-reads safe but a correctly-locked stale value is still stale; add one anyway only if threads share this, since the stat-then-read window is racy
citations.A6: The same mutable dict object is handed to every caller, so one caller's mutation silently edits everyone's config and also desyncs the cache from disk; return a deep copy
citations.A7: before the fix both lines print `{'v': 1}`; after, the second prints `{'v': 2}`
